expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "Do not present a flat 8% per cost centre. With payroll at 68% of opex, a flat cut mostly lands on people." Explains: "A flat 8% on non-payroll yields only 2.6 points. The other 5.4 points ... has to come from people costs" and "It rewards padding and punishes lean teams. Cost centres that already run tight take the same hit as ones with slack."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: Sizes the target (illustrative EUR 6.0M), checks the baseline ("the real underlying cut is closer to 11-12%") and in-year vs run-rate, but never asks what the board actually needs (margin, cash or a covenant); it treats 'opex -8%' as the goal. Margin appears only as a data request ("and the current margin").

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: 'Stop' class: "low-use tools and licences, agency or contractor spend ..., unused office space, events without pipeline ... Cut fully, first." Waterfall: "Non-payroll: vendors, licences, travel, facilities, agency and contractors | 3.0 | About 12% of non-payroll" and "the first two weeks go to proving that EUR 3.0M exists in the ledger."

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: Uses "hiring freeze and non-backfilled attrition" (EUR 1.8M) and a Protect class with criteria ("delivery capacity at healthy utilisation, key account owners, sales pipeline with a short payback"), but the freeze has no exceptions, there are no internal moves or redeployment, and the base plan includes "spans, layers and utilisation-driven resizing of support functions | 0.6 | ... the one lever that carries exit cost" as a planned cut, not a last resort.

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: No leadership pay, bonus or perk measure. The only pay line is general: "Payroll: variable pay, overtime, open requisitions removed from budget | 0.6".

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: The waterfall has amounts and notes and the action list has owners and deadlines, but levers carry no owner or confidence, timing is only loose ("only partly in-year"), there is no list of what stops or waits beyond the class definition, and no remaining gap is shown (the waterfall is set to total 6.0, with Option C as a fallback).

overall_quality.evidence: Sound arithmetic and a clear argument about billable capacity, baseline drift and Dutch process, but a placeholder waterfall without owners, no leaders-first measure and no question about what the board's real target is.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked: 68/32 split arithmetic (2.6 and 5.4 points, 48 FTE at EUR 85k), WMCO threshold of 20 in one UWV area within three months, works council advice before the decision, UWV or settlement route with transition payment. No errors found.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files or internal jargon such as 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt sets a cost target with a thin but positive margin; no bad outcome is described.

best_insight.value: The delivery-cost illustration (cutting EUR 8 of delivery cost that earns 1.25x loses about EUR 10 of revenue) and Option C, asking the board for a phased target if 8% in-year can only come from compulsory redundancies.
best_insight.evidence: 'Why a flat 8%' point 2 and 'Your decision' Option C.

suggestions.assertion: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
suggestions.reason: This sample shows the difference between questioning the baseline (done) and questioning the objective (not done); the assertion text could say so explicitly to make grading consistent.

suggestions.assertion: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples; every reply opened against the flat cut. It does not discriminate. Consider requiring the 'efficient vs wasteful' point to be shown with the user's own numbers or an example.

suggestions.assertion: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten samples. A sharper version would require the no-job levers to be sized in money with a range and shown against the gap, and pricing/leakage kept separate from the opex figure.

No assertion checks in-year versus run-rate phasing of savings and one-off costs under Dutch process (works council advice, WMCO, notice periods). That drove most of the difference in financial soundness between samples.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
suggestions.reason: Compound assertion (amount, timing, owner, confidence, stop list, remaining gap). Several strong samples missed only one element; consider splitting it so partial structure is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Clear and correct but thin: misses the board's real objective, leaders first and a lever-level structure.
